column2: In battle on Sunday there is no fruit; on Monday defeat is quelled; with Mars know quarrel; Mercury for desire; Jupiter
for victory; Venus for the mind; on Saturday defeat in battle. In the Pingala wheel the stars to be given are those the sun occupies:
mouth, eyes, forehead, head, hands, thighs, feet; at the foot, death in three stars; three in the fortnight destroy wealth;
at the mouth, pain; at the head, destruction of the work; in the belly, fruit. I shall tell the Rahu wheel:
from Indra one goes to Nirriti; from Nirriti to Soma; from Soma to Hutashana; from fire to Apya; from Apya to Shiva's abode;
from Rudra to Yama; from Yama to Vayu; from Vayu to the moon again. He consumes four channels; at Rahu's back, victory in battle;
in front, death. I shall tell you the lunar-day Rahu: from Agni to Shiva, from the full moon, beloved:
in the east up to the dark eighth, there is fear when Rahu looks. In the northeast, southeast, southwest and northwest, the serpent Rahu;
Aries and the rest in the east and other directions; where the Sun is in front, death. The third in the dark fortnight, the seventh, tenth,
and fourteenth; and in the bright, the fourth and eleventh days; the fifteenth are Vishti; the full moon in the southeast and northwest.
A, Ka, Cha, Ṭa, Ta, Pa, Ya, Sha — the groups; the Sun and the other planets; vulture, owl, hawk, Pingala, Kaushika in order;
hare, peacock, gorankuh — the birds are remembered. At first the mantra is accomplished, offered; in expulsion, pallava is remembered;
in subjugation, fever and attraction the application brings accomplishment; "Shanta," "Priti," "Namaskara," "Vaushat" in nourishment and subjugation and the like;
Hum in death, destruction of affection; "Phat" in hatred and expulsion; "Vashat" in begetting and kindling; six are the classes of mantras.
I shall tell the herbs that grant great protection: Mahakali, Chandi, Varahi and Ishvari,
Sudarshana and Indrani, worn on the body, protect him; Bala, Atibala, Bhiru, Mushali, Sahadevi,
Jati, Mallika, Yuthi, Garudi, Bhringaraja — the great herbs of wheel form, worn, give victory and the like;
at an eclipse, great goddess, uprooted they give good. Having made an elephant of clay marked with all marks,
having placed it at its feet one should paralyze the enemy of oneself. On a mountain peak, at a single tree, at a spot struck by lightning,

having brought anthill-earth one should join the two mothers: "Om, homage to the great Bhairava of terrible fangs and fierce form, tawny-eyed, bearing trident and sword, vaushat" — one should worship the clay, goddess; one should paralyze the net of weapons.
I shall tell the fire-rite that increases victory in battle and the like: at night in a cremation ground, in a wood fire, a man naked with loose hair,
facing south, should offer human flesh, blood, poison, mixed with husk and bone-pieces, with the enemy's name, eight hundred times:

Om, homage to the revered Kaumari, Lala Lala, play, play, Ghantadevi, kill so-and-so quickly; homage to you, revered knowledge, svaha. By this knowledge, by oblation the enemy comes to bondage. "Om, Vajrakaya, Vajratunda, tawny-yellow, terrible-faced, upward-haired, great-strong, red-faced, lightning-tongued, very fierce, fang-fierce... Hanuman, come, come, the Lord Bhairava commands; come, come, great fierce one, with your long tail wrap so-and-so, wrap, crush, crush, dig, dig, hum phat." The Hanuman rite thirty-eight hundred, goddess, makes all pots.
By the sight of Hanuman on a cloth, enemies come to defeat.
One should write twenty-eight dots, then divided by threes. Then four stars, and one should draw lines there.
In whichever star Rahu stands, that star is on the serpent's head; from it one should place the stars in order of twenty-seven.
When a star falls on the seven at the mouth all die in battle. At the shoulder know defeat, and in the middle seven;
by the one in the belly there is honor and victory for oneself; when a warrior stands at the hip he takes the enemy in battle;
by one at the tail there is fame; death when the star is seen by Rahu. Again I shall tell another, the strength of Sun and Rahu:
Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon, Saturn, Jupiter, Mars and Rahu — these have half-watch shares.
Having put Saturn, Sun and Rahu behind with effort, he conquers an army, a gamble, a journey, battle.
Rohini and the three Uttaras, Mrigashira — five are fixed. Ashvini, Revati, Svati, Dhanishtha and Shatabhisha —
five stars are swift; one who seeks a journey should use them. Anuradha, Hasta, Mula, Mrigashira, Pushya, Punarvasu —
these in all works; Jyeshtha, Chitra and Vishakha; the three Purvas, Agni's, Bharani, Magha, Ardra, Ashlesha are fierce.
In stationary matters a fixed star; in journey a swift one is best; for good fortune only soft ones; in fierce matters fierce ones should be done.
One should do fierce acts in a fierce one; I shall tell the downward-faced and others: Krittika, Bharani, Ashlesha, Vishakha, Pitri, Nirriti;
the three Purvas are downward-faced; one should perform downward-face work. In these: wells, tanks and the like, scholarly work, physician's treatment,
installing, boats, king and the like; likewise digging. Revati, Ashvini, Chitra, Hasta, Svati, Punarvasu,
Anuradha, Mrigashira, Jyeshtha — nine are side-faced. In these a royal consecration, tying the diadem, on elephants and horses,
gardens, houses, temples, enclosures, field arches, banners, signs and flags — one should have all these done.
The twelfth is burnt by the Sun, and likewise the eleventh by the Moon; the tenth burnt by Mars; the third by Mercury;
the sixth burnt by Jupiter; the second by Venus; the seventh by Saturn. Now I shall tell Tripushkara:
the second, twelfth, and seventh with the third; Sunday, Tuesday and Saturday — these six are Tripushkaras.
Vishakha, Krittika, the two Uttaras, Punarvasu and Purva Bhadrapada — these six are Tripushkaras.
Gain, loss, victory, growth, birth of a son, likewise lost, fallen or destroyed — all that becomes threefold.
Ashvini, Bharani, Ashlesha, Pushya, Svati, Vishakha, and Shravana the seventh —
these are firm-eyed and see the ten directions. In journeys, even of one far away, a return arrives in the holy sphere.
Ashadha, Revati, Chitra, Kekarani, Punarvasu: in these five stars the return of one set out occurs.
Krittika, Rohini, Mrigashira, Phalguni and Magha likewise, Mula, Jyeshtha, Anuradha, Dhanishtha, Shatabhisha,
and Purva Bhadrapada — these are the "flattened"; for one going on a road there is again a return.
Hasta, Uttara Bhadrapada, Ardra and Ashadha — lost wealth is seen, there is no battle.
Again I shall tell the Gandanta as it stands in the middle of a star: at the end of Revati four channels, and four at the beginning of Ashvini;
of both one should avoid with effort even a watch's measure. At the end of Ashlesha and beginning of Magha four ghatikas;
the second is called Ganda; hear the third, Bhairavi: between Jyeshtha and Mula a fierce watch;
one should not do auspicious acts if one wishes one's own life; at the time of birth of a child the father and mother die.
Sagittarius, Capricorn and Aquarius — signs of the Sun; the first sign; movable, fixed, dual by nature — Aries and the rest in order.
Cancer, Capricorn, Libra and Aries are movable. One should do movable work, victory, desire, and auspicious and inauspicious;
fixed: Taurus, Leo, Aquarius, Scorpio for fixed work. There is no speedy meeting; the afflicted is not freed.
Gemini, Virgo, Pisces and Sagittarius are dual; the dual ones are auspicious in all works always,
in journey, trade, battle, marriage, seeing a king; one gains growth, victory and profit, and victory in war.
Ashvini has twenty stars shaped like a horse; if it rains there, it rains one night;
when rain is at Yama's star it rains a fortnight.
In the middle of a fort, if benefic planets are with stars again, victory to those in the middle; they know defeat for the one arriving.
At the entering star one should enter; at the departing star one should depart. When Venus, Mercury and Mars all reach the end of a star,
then one should know defeat, and victory for the newcomer. When one begins war in the four stars of entry,
then that fort is conquered; one should not marvel there.
The Saindhavas, Yamunas, Gurjakas, Bhojas, Bahlikas, Jalandhara and Kashmir, and the seventh, Uttarapatha —
these countries perish at the sight of that omen. Hasta, Chitra, Magha, Svati, Mrigashira, and Punarvasu,
Uttara Phalguni and Ashvini likewise — if anything happens here one should indicate the Vayavya group:
all the people lose dharma, cry "Alas," lose their senses; Dahala, Kamarupa, Kalinga and Kosala,
Ayodhya and Avanti perish; Konkana and Andhra. Ashlesha, Mula and Purvashadha likewise,
Revati, the star of Varuna, and Uttara Bhadrapada — if anything stirs here one should indicate it as Varuna's:
cows with abundant milk and ghee, trees with abundant flowers and fruit; health arises there and the earth is rich in crops;
grains are cheap, there is plenty, O king; among kings there will be dreadful war with one another.
Jyeshtha, Rohini, Anuradha, Vishnu's, Dhanishtha, Uttarashadha, and the seventh Abhijit —
if anything falls here one should indicate it as Mahendra's: the people there prosper, free of all disease;
kings make peace; plenty, good for the king. A village should be known as twofold, the great one making face and tail:
if moon, Rahu and sun stand in one sign it is the face-village; in the seventh it is called the tail.
When the moon moves in the fifteenth star from the sun, when a lunar day is cut, one should indicate the Soma-village.
When war has arisen, for whomever the name is declared with a long vowel in the Aditya and Jupiter groups,
victory is his at all times even in terrible battle. When the warrior's name is short, he dies, unstoppable.
The first long at the start, the second in the middle, the last at the end; two by the middle, the first and last are born; no doubt here;
again when at the end or at the beginning the vowel-mounted is seen, one should know death for the short and victory for the long.
I shall tell the human wheel of the nature of the body of stars: one should first draw an image; one should place the stars from the foot.
One should place three on the head, one on the mouth, two stars on the eyes; four on the hands, again two stars on the ears;
